gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the false necessity direction: bare existence of the specular directional derivative does not imply existence of the one-sided derivatives, with oscillatory counterexamples, and therefore cannot support the dependent results without an added one-sided hypothesis.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed equivalence incorrectly infers one-sided directional differentiability and its dependent formulas or estimates from existence of a specular derivative alone.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed necessity direction from existence of the specular derivative to existence of both one-sided derivatives is false, and dependent results must not make that inference.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly states that the only-if direction is false, gives a specularly differentiable function whose forward quotient has no limit, and requires one-sided differentiability as a hypothesis for dependent results.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 concerns the general inference from a bare specular derivative to one-sided derivatives in the characterization theorem. It does not diagnose the distinct quasi-MVT failure that the scaled derivative of ||w||f may be undefined even for an admissible specularly Gateaux differentiable f, nor does it supply that missing existence hypothesis for every relevant w and segment point.

Both entries identify the unsupported lower norm estimate in the quasi-MVT: the scalar argument supplies signed information, which cannot be converted into a lower bound involving derivative magnitudes without an additional sign choice or condition.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof deletes sign information and thereby claims a two-sided norm comparison from a signed scalar quasi-MVT inequality; the infimum/lower estimate is false.

component_coverage.gold_component: The quasi-MVT proof cannot derive the advertised lower bound on the norm of the endpoint difference from signed scalar derivative inequalities; the lower estimate must be deleted or made signed/conditional.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 gives a concrete piecewise-linear counterexample to the infimum norm inequality, explains that only a signed lower bound follows, and proposes replacing the false inequality by a signed statement.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries show that specular gradients are nonlinear under summation: uniform sampling averages component specular gradients, which need not equal the specular gradient of the aggregate objective, invalidating the asserted estimator interface and its convergence proof.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The S-SPEG unbiasedness identity equating the sampled component-gradient expectation with the aggregate specular gradient is false for the advertised finite-sum class.

component_coverage.gold_component: Uniform component sampling does not provide an unbiased estimator of the aggregate specular gradient because specular gradients are not additive.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-008 gives the same |x| and x counterexample, states that the implemented uniform-sampling algorithm is not covered by the defined method, and replaces equality with an appropriate subgradient-membership relation.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the missing upper bound on the specular-gradient norms needed to infer divergence of the normalized step sum, and both explain that bounded iterates plus convexity can supply the bound only after the proof establishes those facts.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The liminf contradiction uses sum h_l=infinity without first proving a uniform bound on the denominators ||nabla^s f(x_l)||.

component_coverage.gold_component: The contradiction argument is unsupported because divergence of the normalized steps requires a prior uniform gradient bound, obtainable from bounded iterates and local boundedness of convex subgradients.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-009 states that H3 alone does not imply divergence of the normalized steps, identifies the missing bounded-gradient argument and its proof-order problem, and supplies the required repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the invalid upgrade from convergence of a sub-subsequence to closeness of every sufficiently late iterate, and both give the correct tail-estimate repair starting at a sufficiently late subsequence index.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Convergence of the selected subsequence does not by itself establish convergence of the full sequence; the tail inequality must start at one suitably late subsequence element.

component_coverage.gold_component: The final convergence step incorrectly transfers subsequence convergence to all later iterates without applying the tail inequality from a suitably chosen subsequence index.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-010 explicitly distinguishes sub-subsequence convergence from full-sequence convergence and specifies choosing a subsequence index before applying the telescoping estimate.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the sample-dependent normalized step as the source of the invalid factorization of the conditional expectation and the resulting failure of the descent inequality, with deterministic steps as a repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Because h_k depends on the sampled component gradient, it cannot be taken outside the conditional expectation; the expected normalized direction need not be a subgradient direction.

component_coverage.gold_component: The normalized stochastic step makes the step length sample-dependent, invalidating the conditional-expectation factorization and the claimed descent/convergence estimate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-012 explicitly states that h_l depends on the sampled index, cannot be factored from expectation, gives a normalized-direction counterexample, and proposes deterministic step sizes.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-009 concerns proving divergence of normalized step lengths through bounded gradients and the resulting liminf argument. It does not recognize the separate invalid inference from a weighted sum of expected objective gaps to a pointwise or unspecified-iterate expectation bound.
